lines.text: A volcanic island and a chain of small ones in the eastern Caribbean, home of the Garifuna and of La Soufriere. This is Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
In the eighteenth century Kingstown grew up on the south coast of Saint Vincent, and it is the capital still.
The Garifuna held the island for a long time. After the war of the mid seventeen nineties, the British deported them to Central America.
Milton Cato would lead the islands to independence and become their first prime minister.
James Mitchell would serve as prime minister for sixteen years, from 1984 to 2000.
Ralph Gonsalves would follow, and lead the country for almost a quarter of a century.
Kevin Lyttle took the island's sound to the world in 2003, with his hit Turn Me On.
In 1979, months after La Soufriere erupted, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines became independent from Britain.
In 2024 Hurricane Beryl tore through the Grenadines and wrecked Union Island.
Shaped by volcano and storm, these small islands have kept their own way.
